trees.objective: Mesurer la combinaison des variantes actuellement les plus rapides de T1 et T2 : ordonnancement OpenMP dynamic,2 et chemin AABB avec sélection des bornes par dirIsNeg pour les inverses finis. Valider tous les contrôles et mesurer à 1, 4 et 40 threads. Comparer au meilleur résultat actuel Gm2, sans supposer que les gains s’additionnent.

trees.subject: Intégration des variantes récentes OpenMP et AABB

trees.objective: Explore a one-CTA loop that reduces the entire input and writes directly to out, with no scratch or intermediate launches. Compare end-to-end latency at n=4,194,304 against the existing multistage path, as well as at the other valid sizes to find any general crossover. Preserve bounds and exact results. Treat this as a distinct architectural contrast even if it is slower; the kernel may be useful in a later combination.
trees.subject: Single-CTA full-array reduction and size crossover

trees.objective: Tune the block reduction implementation while holding the baseline per-CTA input tile, partial counts, recursive launch graph, and output copy fixed. Explore thread mapping, register accumulation within that fixed tile, and warp/block reduction methods; use wider loads only when alignment and bounds permit. Compare full-run latency at n=4,194,304 and validate all supplied sizes, including exact accumulation.
trees.subject: Intra-CTA reduction primitive with fixed topology

trees.objective: With one reduction primitive held fixed, explore multi-CTA hierarchies for n=4,194,304: vary general tile sizes and partial counts, and compare the current recursive graph with fewer-stage alternatives. Explicitly compare a final CTA folding all remaining partials and writing out against adding a parallel tail stage. Measure complete-run latency and validate correctness for all valid n; do not rely on initialized scratch or unsafe cross-CTA synchronization. The fixed primitive separates these schedule experiments from T2, while later integration may combine their results.
trees.subject: Large-input hierarchy and final-tail alternatives

trees.objective: In src/candidate.cu, explore large-input hierarchical reduction for n=4194304. Replace the current modulo-based interleaved reduction and repeated block-wide synchronization with an efficient warp/block reduction approach, while having CTAs accumulate multiple values per thread from coalesced, disjoint input tiles. Write partials to bounded scratch and reduce them directly to out. Tune tile and block configuration; compare a two-stage path with an additional final reduction stage if the partial count makes a single final CTA inefficient. Cover all legal sizes with bounded reads, exact int32 output, unchanged ABI/default stream, and a correct fallback. Compare all checks and repeated timings against the baseline.
trees.subject: Large-input hierarchical reduction and warp/block reduction costs

trees.objective: In src/candidate.cu, explore a generic size-based single-CTA reduction that writes directly to out for small inputs, eliminating intermediate partials and the final device copy where beneficial. Measure crossover thresholds rather than hardcoding test sizes. Explicitly compare against the baseline n=1 device-to-device copy path, which launches no kernel, and retain whichever path measures better. Keep a correct fallback for larger inputs and preserve correctness, bounded reads, exact int32 results, ABI, and default-stream behavior for every legal size. Compare all checks and repeated timings.
trees.subject: Small-input direct-output reduction and launch crossover

trees.objective: In src/candidate.cu, evaluate a large-input alternative with an ordered output-zeroing kernel followed by a multi-CTA grid-stride reduction; each CTA reduces its own values and performs one int32 atomicAdd to out. Tune CTA count/work per CTA to balance input throughput against contention. Do not rely on initialized scratch or unsafe inter-block initialization. Preserve exact results, bounds, ABI, default-stream ordering, and a correct fallback for other legal sizes; compare all checks and repeated timings against the baseline and hierarchical approach.
trees.subject: Large-input atomic final aggregation

trees.objective: Mesurer une combinaison qui conserve la voie atomique T3 pour les grandes tailles et reprend la voie directe T2 seulement aux tailles où elle est pertinente. Préserver la correction pour toute taille légale et comparer la latence de n=4194304 à la source T3.
trees.stop_condition: Rejeter la combinaison si elle échoue aux contrôles ou si sa moyenne répétée à n=4194304 n’est pas inférieure à celle de T3; conserver alors T3.

trees.objective: Optimize y and gx as separate kernels; do not fuse them. Contrast a flat or coarsened output mapping that reduces CTAs and inactive lanes with cooperative reuse of inputs across neighboring outputs, such as a tiled stencil with shared halo data. Preserve the specified forward equation and its exact derivative, including padding; for gx, use gx[s] = sum_j gy[s-j+floor(K/2)]*k[j], rather than relying on an odd-K-only index identity. Validate supported dimensions and compare full-call latency.

trees.objective: Test a fused y/gx kernel as a distinct alternative to T1’s separate kernels. Evaluate whether shared row scheduling or coefficient reuse offsets fusion’s resource costs, and compare full-call latency against the best available separate-kernel control, not only the original baseline. Compute the exact derivative of the specified forward equation, including for even K if supported; preserve fresh, independent outputs and validate correctness.
trees.subject: Compare fused forward/input-gradient computation against optimized separate kernels

trees.objective: Parallelize gk’s B*L reduction and contrast a cooperative reduction within one CTA per (h,j) with scratch-backed tiled partial sums and a final reduction. Measure the complete call, including any extra launches or resets; write every scratch value before consuming it and avoid stale-output accumulation. Preserve the specified padding and gk tolerance for supported dimensions.
trees.subject: Compare kernel-gradient reduction strategies and their full-call costs

trees.objective: Own the separate forward and input-gradient kernels and their launch mapping in src/candidate.cu. Explore packing multiple short rows per CTA and other coalesced, well-utilized mappings to reduce inactive threads and CTA overhead; keep the two passes separate so this tree isolates mapping/kernel-efficiency gains from fusion. Preserve bounds-safe zero padding, full FP32, all-input correctness, complete output writes, and the fixed API. Judge candidates by correctness and full-call timing, not an assumed per-kernel benefit.
trees.subject: Improve forward and input-gradient CTA mapping without fusion

trees.objective: Own the forward/input-gradient execution path in src/candidate.cu. Test a fused kernel that computes y and gx together, sharing coordinate/filter handling where beneficial; measure whether fewer launches and shared work outweigh increased register use or reduced occupancy. Do not modify the weight-gradient path. Preserve full FP32, zero-padding semantics, all-input correctness and tolerances, complete fresh writes to both outputs, and the fixed API. Compare complete-call timing and report measured results rather than assuming fusion helps.
trees.subject: Measure a fused forward and input-gradient kernel

trees.objective: Own the weight-gradient kernel and its use of scratch in src/candidate.cu. Compare reduction granularities rather than assuming multi-stage partial sums win: test a CTA-level reduction distributed across B*L for each (h,j), and, where useful, split B*L into tiles that write partial sums to scratch followed by a final reduction. You may also test tiling neighboring j outputs if it enables useful reuse. Use no extra allocations; every scratch read must follow a write in the current call, and all outputs must be freshly written. Preserve bounds, the contracted gradient, full FP32, and the required tolerances for all valid inputs. Judge variants by correctness and complete-call timing, since the supplied baseline timing does not attribute cost to this kernel.
trees.subject: Compare one-stage and split weight-gradient reductions

trees.objective: Partir du programme T3, le plus rapide mesuré, et y intégrer le mapping séparé des kernels forward et input-gradient de T1. Conserver la réduction gk de T3. Mesurer le programme complet et vérifier la correction; ne pas présumer que les gains s’additionnent.

trees.objective: Partir de b957, qui regroupe quatre sorties gk par CTA, et y intégrer uniquement le mapping séparé forward/input-gradient de f014. Ces changements visent des kernels distincts; mesurer la combinaison complète sans présumer d’un gain additif.
trees.stop_condition: Ne retenir que si la combinaison est correcte et bat 0,00940615 s en moyenne sur l’appel complet; sinon garder b957 pour la sélection finale.
trees.subject: Intégrer le mapping T1 au kernel gk b957

trees.objective: Construire des variantes SIMT FP32 en séparant d’abord l’effet du mapping de celui de la réutilisation : comparer le kernel naïf à un kernel direct sans mémoire partagée, mais avec les colonnes row-major contiguës affectées aux lanes, puis à un kernel synchrone à tuiles partagées. Après ce contrôle, explorer réutilisation A/B, accumulateurs en registres et dimensions de tuiles, seuls ou combinés. Appliquer alpha et beta une seule fois, préserver l’exactitude FP32 et les bords, ne pas ajouter d’allocation et produire C pour toutes les tailles. Rapporter correction et temps répétés pour chaque variante sur le cas 4096.
trees.subject: Mapping coalescé, puis réutilisation et tuilage SIMT FP32

trees.objective: Pour isoler le mécanisme de chargement, comparer d’abord un kernel SIMT FP32 synchrone et sa variante TMA avec le même mapping de sortie, les mêmes tuiles et le même calcul; mesurer l’effet de TMA et de la profondeur du pipeline avant de modifier ces autres paramètres. Vérifier la faisabilité cible/CUDA 12.6.3, la synchronisation, les alignements et les bords; conserver alpha/beta et le calcul FP32 complet sans allocation supplémentaire. Ensuite, explorer le réglage ou la combinaison des variantes si les mesures le justifient. Rapporter correction et temps répétés sur le cas 4096, ainsi que tout obstacle de compatibilité.
trees.subject: Comparaison contrôlée du chargement TMA asynchrone sur Hopper

trees.objective: First benchmark a minimal coalesced, row-major one-output-per-thread kernel with lanes varying over columns, to isolate the cost of the supplied baseline’s lane mapping. Then explore synchronous shared-memory CTA tiles using that coalesced orientation and one output per thread, varying tile dimensions and K depth. Support tails and all valid dimensions and values, compute every output with the requested alpha/beta semantics, and report correctness and repeated timing. Use full-FP32 CUDA-core arithmetic only; preserve the entry point and buffer/stream constraints, with no extra allocations or external math libraries.
trees.subject: Coalescing control plus synchronous SIMT CTA tiling

trees.objective: Focus on register-blocked SIMT where each thread maintains multiple independent FP32 output accumulators, testing distinct row/column microtile mappings to reuse operands and improve arithmetic intensity. Compare against a one-output-per-thread control so the result is not merely a CTA tile-size comparison with T1; measure register/occupancy tradeoffs and correctness as well as repeated timing. Support tails and all valid dimensions and values, apply alpha/beta once per output, and preserve the entry point, buffers, stream, and full-FP32 requirement. Do not use tensor-core/reduced-precision math, extra allocations, or external math libraries.
trees.subject: Multi-accumulator register-blocked SIMT microtiles

trees.objective: Explore whether asynchronous global-to-shared K-stage copies improve a tiled SIMT kernel. Establish a paired synchronous-staging control with the same CTA tile, lane mapping, and compute mapping as the asynchronous version, then compare timings and correctness to isolate the pipeline effect. Handle alignment, completion, synchronization, tails, and any needed fallback for all valid inputs; preserve full-FP32 arithmetic, alpha/beta semantics, entry point, stream, and buffer limits. Use only CUDA 12.6.3-supported mechanisms, no external math libraries, reduced precision, or extra allocations; treat gains as hypotheses to measure.
trees.subject: Matched synchronous/asynchronous K-stage pipeline comparison

trees.objective: Tester l’ajout du staging partagé synchrone 16×16/K=16 de T3 au noyau registre de T2, qui calcule quatre lignes par thread et réutilise B. Partir de T2, préserver ses accès coalescés et calculs FP32, puis vérifier la correction et mesurer si le staging partagé réduit le temps.
trees.stop_condition: Rejeter le composé s’il échoue en correction ou n’améliore pas de façon répétable le meilleur temps valide de T2; toute amélioration doit encore être confirmée indépendamment avant de retenir G.
trees.subject: Tuilage partagé synchrone avec microtuiles registre

trees.objective: À partir du candidat T2 valide (tuile CTA 8×128, microtuile registre 2×4), explorer différents ordres de parcours des tuiles CTA ou regroupements de blocs afin d’améliorer la localité cache et la réutilisation des opérandes. Garder calcul, microtuile et arithmétique FP32 fixes pour isoler l’effet du parcours; préserver la correction et les contraintes de stockage.
trees.stop_condition: Arrêter si la variante échoue en correction ou ne bat pas de façon répétable 11,853 ms.
trees.subject: Ordre de parcours CTA et localité cache

trees.objective: In src/candidate.py, investigate a shape-generic, single-kernel Triton softmax using full-row tiles. Explicitly contrast one program per row with viable grouped-row mappings (for example, multiple independent rows per CTA with a suitable warp-per-row layout), and tune layout/warp count. Derive dimensions from x, mask non-power-of-two widths and any grouped-row tail, preserve stable FP32 max-exp-sum normalization, and allocate no scratch beyond the output. Optimize for 4096x4096 without specializing to correctness-test values. Avoid torch.softmax; validate all required shapes and independent random inputs against the stated tolerance. Compare against the naive reference and official tutorial with the exact do_bench protocol, including allocations and host launches and excluding JIT warmup; report failures as well as results.
trees.subject: Full-row fused softmax with row-mapping contrast

trees.objective: In src/candidate.py, investigate a distinct one-program-per-row online softmax that processes bounded chunks rather than retaining a full row tile. For each chunk, combine its local maximum and exponential sum with the running maximum/sum using stable rescaling; make a second traversal to write normalized exponentials. Tune chunk size and warp count, use masks for tails, and allocate no scratch beyond the output. This trades rereads for lower live per-program state; test whether it helps the 4096-column case. Preserve FP32 stability, support general dimensions, avoid torch.softmax, validate all required shapes and independent random inputs to the stated tolerance, compare using the exact do_bench protocol, and record failures as well as successful measurements.
trees.subject: Chunked online low-register Triton softmax

trees.objective: Implement the direct, non-streaming Triton design with one program/CTA owning one complete row: masked load, stable max/exp/sum, and normalized store. Compare with the official tutorial and explore configurations for this one-row mapping only. Do not switch to multi-row CTAs or streaming loops. Support arbitrary valid widths and tails, preserve the stated accuracy and input/output requirements, and retain only correctness-passing measured improvements.
trees.subject: Direct fused one-row-per-CTA kernel

trees.objective: Test CTAs that compute multiple independent complete rows using per-row reductions. Explore rows-per-CTA and only the layout/warp choices needed for this grouped mapping; do not repeat T1’s one-row configuration search or use streaming or split-row algorithms. Compare against T1’s best measured direct one-row result and the official candidates. Support arbitrary valid shapes and tails and preserve the stated accuracy and input/output requirements.
trees.subject: Grouped multi-row-per-CTA kernel

trees.objective: Explore a single-CTA-per-row streaming softmax that processes column tiles while maintaining a numerically stable running maximum and rescaled sum, then rereads tiles to produce normalized output. This tests whether reducing live per-row state outweighs extra input traffic for the performance shape. Support arbitrary widths and tails, preserve the stated accuracy and input/output requirements, and retain the approach only if official measurements justify it.
trees.subject: Streaming online reduction to reduce live row state

trees.objective: À partir du meilleur candidat T1, intégrer le noyau T2 à plusieurs lignes par CTA comme alternative sélectionnée selon des dimensions génériques, sans seuil calé sur les seules formes de test. Garder le noyau direct comme option pour les lignes larges; préserver le softmax stable, les masques de queue, la correction et les contraintes d’entrée/sortie, sans intermédiaire supplémentaire. Mesurer le programme intégré selon le protocole officiel.

trees.subject: Intégration mesurée des mappings direct et groupé

trees.objective: In src/candidate.cpp, explore OpenMP parallelization while retaining the scalar stencil expression. Compare serial versus parallel output initialization separately from parallel stencil updates, and compare a persistent region across timesteps with per-step regions if useful. Respect threads as a hard budget, avoid oversubscription, and synchronize dependent timesteps. Measure total runtime on one and four cores, verify full outputs and boundaries on correctness cases, and record failed approaches. Keep SIMD and temporal blocking out of isolated measurements.

Handle unaligned row offsets, arbitrary interior widths and scalar tails; do not assume unsupported ISA or alter the six-step/buffer semantics. Keep execution within the threads budget, check the fixed numerical tolerance, and measure one and four cores. Record failed approaches and results.
trees.subject: SIMD vectorization of the x-axis stencil

Sweep a few tile sizes and temporal depths; for depth d preserve the radius-3d dependency halo, alternating-buffer state, and fixed boundaries, writing only validated tile interiors. Test correctness and native wall time at one and four cores, including initialization and overhead.

Do not change compiler settings or assume row alignment; handle tails and generic n. Preserve the recurrence, full initialization, and boundaries, and validate the fixed tolerance. Measure both core budgets and include any setup costs.

Compare a spatial-only tiled control with a halo-aware multi-step tile, holding the spatial kernel and threading strategy fixed within the comparison to isolate temporal reuse. Respect radius-three dependencies, produce both full output buffers with baseline initialization and boundaries, and include scratch allocation in timing. Avoid benchmark-size specialization; validate correctness and measure one- and four-core wall time.

Partir du candidat T2 le plus rapide; éviter le parallélisme imbriqué, conserver les barrières entre pas, respecter threads et toutes les contraintes de correction. Conserver les bénéfices mesurés du parcours par lignes et de l’équipe OpenMP persistante, sans modifier le compilateur ni supposer un alignement ou une taille fixes. Vérifier la tolérance et mesurer à un et quatre cœurs, tous coûts inclus.

Évaluer la combinaison à un et quatre cœurs contre Gm1 et ses parents, sans présumer que leurs gains s’additionnent; préserver la correction et les contraintes du protocole.

Reproduce the baseline y-halo mapping for every offset, produce all 64³ outputs from current A on every call, and use no extra launch or allocation. Validate against the independent oracle and compare full-run event latency with the baseline.

Explore a small number of outputs per thread and suitable launch geometry; preserve exact coefficients and baseline halo mapping, compute every output from current A, and use no additional allocation or launch. Compare oracle correctness and full-run latency.

Preserve the ABI and default stream, support every n, and avoid out-of-bounds reads or assumptions about scratch contents.

Tune the partial count and final reduction while measuring both launches together. Write every partial before reading it; do not depend on scratch initialization or require output atomics. Preserve the ABI and default stream, support every n, and avoid out-of-bounds reads.

Explore global work partitioning: vary first-stage partial count/granularity and the finalizer’s fan-in so the large input is sufficiently parallel while finalization stays cheap. Prendre une tuile partagée conflict-free, par exemple 32x33, comme hypothèse de départ plutôt que comme obligation ; comparer si utile des géométries CTA et du travail scalaire ou vectorisé par thread. Préserver l’API, le flux par défaut, l’absence d’allocation et la copie bit-exacte de toutes les valeurs. Vérifier la correction à n=32,64,256,1024 et comparer des temps répétés de l’exécution complète à n=1024 sur la cible fixée, sans présumer qu’un accès nominalement coalescé sera plus rapide.
trees.subject: Transposition tuilée et coalesçage des accès globaux

trees.objective: Évaluer comme approche alternative un échange de valeurs par registres et lanes, avec les shuffles comme une possibilité, afin de voir si les accès globaux peuvent être coalescés à moindre coût de synchronisation ou de mémoire partagée. Ne pas exiger une solution exclusivement intra-warp : tester une variante hybride si l’échange entre warps ou une permutation différente est nécessaire. Préserver les bits FP32, valider la participation et les masques des lanes, tester toutes les dimensions de correction et mesurer à n=1024 avec des répétitions comparables. Rapporter aussi un résultat négatif si le coût des échanges ou des transferts annule le bénéfice attendu.
trees.subject: Échange des données par registres et lanes : voie alternative ou hybride

trees.objective: Isoler l’effet de l’ordre des blocs sur une transposition tuilée correcte à accès coalescés. Dans cette branche indépendante, établir un contrôle row-major, puis garder fixes son code intra-CTA, sa géométrie et son mapping de données pendant la comparaison avec un remappage diagonal ou une autre permutation bijective des CTAs. Comparer sur les grilles correspondant aux dimensions valides. Traiter un effet éventuel sur la localité, le cache ou les partitions mémoire comme une hypothèse à mesurer, pas comme un fait ; conserver le changement seulement s’il passe les tests exacts et améliore les mesures répétées de l’exécution complète à n=1024.
trees.subject: Ordre des blocs : expérience contrôlée sur une transposition tuilée

trees.objective: Own only src/candidate.cu. Replace the baseline's strided global stores with a single-pass shared-memory tiled transpose: load input rows coalesced, exchange tile orientation in shared memory, then store output rows coalesced. Compare the padded 32x33 scalar tile with at least one meaningfully different shared-memory layout or multi-element/vectorized thread-ownership variant; do not presume the padded scalar layout is fastest on this target. Measure the complete run at n=1024. Preserve the run entry point and exact bit patterns; produce every C element for every positive n multiple of 32, pass correctness at n=32, 64, 256, and 1024, use no new allocation or other file edits, and report build, correctness, and repeated timing evidence.
trees.subject: Shared-memory transpose layouts and ownership

trees.objective: Own only src/candidate.cu. Independently explore a warp-register transpose using warp lane permutations/shuffles to turn coalesced input loads into coalesced output stores, aiming to avoid CTA shared-memory staging and its block-wide synchronization. Design and describe element ownership so each shuffle exchange uses data held by participating lanes in the same warp; do not assume a warp shuffle exchanges data across warps. Tune the warp's element ownership and tile mapping, and report register/spill evidence if present in the ordinary build output. Preserve exact bitwise copies and the run entry point, produce all output for every positive n multiple of 32, pass the required correctness sizes, allocate no new storage, and report repeated full-run n=1024 timing evidence.
trees.subject: Warp-local register/shuffle transpose

trees.objective: In src/candidate.cpp only, compare two block-oriented alternatives: a full SIMD validator checking byte classes, continuation relationships, and restricted second-byte ranges; and a hybrid that skips all-ASCII blocks using word/SIMD detection but falls back to the existing strict scalar validator for blocks containing non-ASCII bytes. Measure the alternatives separately so benefits are not presumed additive. Handle sequences crossing blocks and tails without reading beyond n, and use only instructions supported by the fixed build target. Preserve the run ABI, full uint32 output, input immutability, and thread budget; do not add parallel work for the one-core case. Validate empty and short inputs, boundary positions, valid ASCII and mixed-width data, and malformed continuations, overlong encodings, surrogates, out-of-range values, and truncations. Record unsuccessful variants. Compare repeated timings on the official workload under the unchanged protocol; treat ASCII and malformed cases as correctness checks unless the official protocol specifies otherwise.
trees.subject: Full SIMD and hybrid ASCII-block UTF-8 paths

trees.objective: In src/candidate.cpp only, explore a scalar control-flow alternative for the complete validator, such as a compact state-machine/table-driven scan, with branch and lookup costs measured rather than presumed. Keep this distinct from a SIMD lane-validation implementation; preserve strict Unicode scalar-value rejection, correct handling of every sequence and end-of-input boundary, no overreads, the existing ABI, complete uint32 output, read-only input, and the threads budget. Run the same malformed and valid correctness checks and unchanged repeated 65,536-byte performance measurements; record failed approaches as well as the best result.
trees.subject: Scalar state-machine and branch-cost optimization

trees.objective: Primary hypothesis: SIMD masks validate UTF-8 constraints across the whole buffer, unlike T2's ASCII-span locator. Explore block classification, shifted continuation requirements, restricted second-byte checks, cross-block state, and a bounded tail. Compare relevant SIMD variants only when supported by the frozen target and unchanged build; do not alter flags or add runtime environment probing. Keep the supplied scalar implementation as a control, and report any useful hybrid as a distinct variant rather than excluding it. Preserve exact scalar-value validation, ABI, output, and thread budget. Use the official mixed-width n=65536 timing for performance and official ASCII/malformed checks for correctness, paying particular attention to vector boundaries and truncations where covered. Record failed variants.
trees.subject: Whole-stream SIMD UTF-8 validation with cross-block state

trees.objective: Primary hypothesis: vector high-bit scans can skip ASCII spans while the existing strict scalar decoder handles non-ASCII code points. The benefit depends on the actual official mixed-width input containing useful ASCII spans; do not assume this or use synthetic-only results as evidence for the scored workload. Start decoding at a known code-point boundary and treat the first high-bit byte as input to validate—not as an assumed lead, since it may be a stray continuation. Keep loads and tails within n. Preserve exact validity, ABI, output, and thread budget. Measure the official mixed-width n=65536 workload and run the official ASCII/malformed correctness checks, especially for boundaries. Report this approach separately from T1's whole-buffer validation; label any hybrid distinctly and record failed variants.
trees.subject: SIMD-assisted ASCII-run skipping with a scalar slow path

trees.objective: Primary hypothesis: reducing scalar decoding control flow or dependencies helps the mixed-width workload; the supplied baseline already has an ASCII fast path, so do not assume ASCII scanning is the only scalar cost. Compare the baseline decoder with compact-state/DFA or reduced-branch scalar variants, measuring each under the official mixed-width n=65536 workload and checking official ASCII/malformed correctness. Keep scalar decoding as the focus, but do not treat that focus as a ban on useful correctness-preserving experiments; label any hybrid separately from pure-scalar results. Preserve exact validity, ABI, output, bounds, and thread budget. Report failed variants.
trees.subject: Branch-reduced scalar UTF-8 decoding

trees.objective: Starting from the fastest correct source 31112, retain its 16-byte SSE2 ASCII-prefix scan and test replacing its scalar suffix with T1's measured 8-byte ASCII-word/mixed-block decoder from 1bef. This tests whether skipping ASCII blocks after the first non-ASCII block helps without sacrificing the faster prefix. Preserve all correctness and protocol constraints; remeasure the combined program and do not assume additive gains.
trees.stop_condition: Reject the integration on any correctness failure or if its official mixed-width mean is not faster than 39.98 µs.
trees.subject: Test a faster ASCII-prefix scan with a word-scanned scalar suffix

trees.objective: Compare bounded OpenMP worksharing strategies across pixels or rows, including contiguous/static work and chunked dynamic or guided work, rather than assuming per-pixel imbalance is important. Keep the single-thread scalar path as a control, and ensure the team never exceeds the supplied `threads` budget regardless of the runtime environment. Preserve the ABI, read-only inputs and full output overwrite. Measure at 1, 4 and 40 threads, and validate the official scaled-camera and modified-density cases; retain failed schedules as results.
trees.subject: Bounded OpenMP parallelism across output pixels

trees.objective: Treat reuse of volume-coordinate scales, strides, and indexing, and a possible interior-sample fast path, as hypotheses for reducing repeated `Density`/`D` cost. Keep the trilinear sampling positions, contributing voxels, edge behavior and ray-march/shadow sampling quality correct, but do not require identical floating-point operation order where the official tolerance is met. Use the unchanged density path as a control so results can be distinguished from shadow-path changes. Measure at all official thread budgets and validate the supplied scaled-camera and modified-density cases; record failed variants.
trees.subject: Reduce per-sample density interpolation overhead

trees.objective: Isolate shadow-path setup and control-flow experiments from the shared `Density` sampler initially. Compare the general transmittance path with mathematically valid reuse or specialization based on the renderer’s fixed light and volume geometry. You may test eliminations of work only when its contribution is provably zero and the result still meets the official tolerance; do not use approximate density cutoffs or lower sampling quality for nonzero contributions. Preserve a baseline-shadow control, measure at 1, 4 and 40 threads, and validate all supplied correctness cases. Record correct but standalone-slower variants if they provide a useful basis for later combination.
trees.subject: Reduce repeated shadow-transmittance setup cost

trees.objective: Separate packetization gains from T1’s scheduling gains: compare the scalar control and any compiler-supported vectorization first, then test packet SIMD across adjacent rays if supported by the frozen build. Do not assume an ISA from the CPU model or change compiler flags. Handle differing march termination and tail pixels correctly, preserving sampling quality and the full output. Measure both a one-thread control and the official 1, 4 and 40 thread budgets so any later combination with worksharing can be judged. Validate all supplied correctness cases and retain reusable, correct variants for consideration even if packetization alone is slower; record build and performance failures.
trees.subject: Vectorize independent rays with divergence-safe SIMD

trees.objective: Explorer le partage parallèle des pixels dans volume_serial, en utilisant threads comme maximum d’équipe et en comparant une distribution de lignes ou d’itérations adaptée au coût variable des rayons. Garder les écritures sans course, couvrir chaque pixel exactement une fois et préserver le chemin à un thread. Valider la correction et comparer les mesures à 1, 4 et 40 cœurs.
trees.subject: Parallélisation OpenMP du rendu par pixel

trees.objective: Explorer le calcul de Density en comparant une voie sans copie — facteurs de coordonnées, indices et accès plats — à une éventuelle préparation par appel d’un volume à halo/clamp, en comptant intégralement allocation et préparation dans le temps mesuré. Préserver les dimensions arbitraires, les bornes inclusives, la conversion des coordonnées en indices, le clamp et l’ordre d’interpolation; ne retenir une préparation que si son coût total est compensé. Vérifier la tolérance sur les densités et résolutions requises et mesurer chaque variante isolément.
trees.subject: Arithmétique et organisation des accès du sampler Density

trees.objective: Cibler la traversée des rayons, en particulier la préparation/intersection des rayons d’ombre et les mises à jour de position, paramètre et contrôle dans transmittance et raymarch. Chercher à réduire le surcoût de contrôle et de calcul scalaire sans réécrire l’interpolation de Density, afin de distinguer cette piste de T2. Conserver la séquence des échantillons, les pas, l’accumulation, l’atténuation et l’arrêt anticipé; évaluer correction et temps séparément puis dans une combinaison mesurée.
trees.subject: Surcoût de traversée et de contrôle des rayons

trees.objective: Mesurer la combinaison du rendu parallèle par pixels de T1, de la variante Density de T2 et de la variante de traversée de T3, en partant de la meilleure source mesurée. Valider la correction et comparer selon le protocole officiel; ne présumer aucun gain additif.
trees.stop_condition: Ne retenir la combinaison que si elle reste correcte et améliore le score officiel face à la meilleure entrée. Ne demander une autre combinaison que si son hypothèse est distincte et que le budget protégé de confirmation reste suffisant.
trees.subject: Intégration mesurée des pistes parallélisme, Density et traversée

trials.hypothesis: The current run path ignores its thread budget and renders scanlines serially; row-level work can also be imbalanced because lower image regions generate many more ambient rays. A serial branch for one thread plus flattened pixels scheduled in dynamic chunks should use the requested OpenMP budget and distribute expensive pixels more evenly. Counter-indexed SplitMix-style samples remove shared drand48 state and make each primary sample reproducible regardless of scheduling, while changing the noise sequence remains subject to the fixed RMSE and mean-difference checks.

retained: Replace shared drand48 state with deterministic counter-indexed SplitMix-style samples, assigning distinct sample indices to each primary subsample and ambient ray.
Render each flattened pixel independently and write all three output channels exactly once.
Use a serial loop for thread budgets of one or less; for larger budgets, use OpenMP dynamic scheduling with 32-pixel chunks and the requested thread count when OpenMP is enabled.

trials.hypothesis: AO needs only an occlusion flag, but the existing full Isect routines also maintain nearest-hit state and construct hit positions and sphere normals. Replacing AO intersections with boolean tests that preserve the original D>0, near-root, positive-t, 1e17 limit, and plane parallel threshold should remove that unused work. This candidate still tests every primitive per AO ray to isolate state reduction from early-exit effects.

retained: Add AO-only sphere and plane boolean hit predicates preserving the original thresholds and near-root semantics.
Use the predicates for ambient rays without constructing or updating full Isect hit state.
Keep all primitive tests, 8x8 AO rays, random draws, and the primary-ray path unchanged.

trials.hypothesis: Replacing the separate sinf/cosf evaluations with GCC 14.2's paired __builtin_sincosf may share argument reduction and reduce AO direction trig cost. The drand48 calls, their order, theta/phi calculation, sample count, and direction scaling remain unchanged, isolating the trig substitution on the same deterministic uniform draws; the performance and numerical impact remain unmeasured.

retained: Replace separate cosf(phi) and sinf(phi) calls with GCC's paired __builtin_sincosf(phi, &sin_phi, &cos_phi), then retain the existing cosine/sine scaling by theta.

trials.hypothesis: The parent already uses AO-specific boolean predicates, but still tests all three spheres and the plane for every ambient ray. Since AO consumes only whether any primitive occluded the ray, stopping at the first sphere hit and testing the plane only after all sphere misses should preserve the hit flag while reducing predicate work on occluded rays. The benefit depends on hit frequency and branch cost, so this is a distinct, unmeasured traversal experiment.

retained: Retain the AO-specific sphere and plane boolean predicates and their original hit thresholds and near-root semantics.
Break the sphere traversal after the first confirmed AO occlusion; test the plane only if all spheres miss.
Keep all 8x8 AO rays, random draws, primary-ray intersection logic, and image-update behavior unchanged.

trials.hypothesis: The prior candidate f658a399cd2a4d16 was valid at 0.45118 s and passed all six RMSE/mean-difference checks, versus the valid baseline at 3.47790 s; the catalog still contains only one distinct candidate, so that result does not isolate scheduling or RNG effects. This contrasting experiment tests cyclic static row assignment with one independently seeded PCG32 stream per worker. Static,1 may distribute vertically varying row costs without dynamic scheduling overhead, while the serial path avoids OpenMP overhead at a one-thread budget. The new stream arrangement may preserve the checks while avoiding sample-indexed generation, but the controller must measure it.

retained: Replace shared drand48 state with worker-local PCG32 streams using distinct odd stream increments and deterministic worker-specific initialization.
Use a serial row loop for thread budgets of one or less; otherwise distribute rows cyclically with OpenMP schedule(static, 1) and the requested thread count when OpenMP is enabled.
Accumulate each pixel locally and assign all three output channels once, retaining all primary subsamples and 8x8 ambient rays.

trials.hypothesis: The prior GCC __builtin_sincosf candidate compiled and passed correctness but was slightly slower than baseline in its three-sample result. This contrasting implementation uses the paired sincosf library entry point, which may share angle reduction differently. Because only the trig evaluation changes, the same ordered drand48 draws produce the same theta and phi inputs; whether it helps remains unmeasured.

retained: Replace the separate cosf(phi) and sinf(phi) calls with the paired sincosf(phi, &sin_phi, &cos_phi) library entry point; keep the existing theta scaling and all sampling unchanged.

trials.hypothesis: The two distinct measured candidates were both valid: cyclic static rows with per-worker PCG streams averaged 0.4134 s, while flattened dynamic chunks with sample-indexed RNG averaged 0.4512 s. Since both scheduling and RNG differed, that comparison does not isolate cause. This candidate keeps per-worker PCG streams and the one-thread serial path, but tests flattened static blocks of eight pixels against cyclic static rows. Interleaved contiguous blocks may spread row-dependent work across workers without dynamic dispatch overhead; the controller must measure the result and verify all fixed correctness checks.

retained: Replace shared drand48 state with invocation-local PCG32 streams, using distinct worker stream selectors and conversion to uniform [0,1) float samples.
Use a serial renderer for thread budgets of one or less; otherwise, when OpenMP is enabled, parallelize a flattened pixel loop with schedule(static, 8) and the requested thread count.
Accumulate each pixel's subsample values locally and assign all three image channels once; retain the original primary-ray and 8x8 ambient-ray counts.

trials.hypothesis: Prior AO-predicate trials were correct but their three-repeat means (3.4749 s for testing all predicates and 3.4643 s with spheres-first early exit, versus 3.4779 s baseline) are too close to establish a benefit. This contrasting variant tests plane-first AO-only predicates: when the plane occludes a ray, it can skip all sphere tests, while sphere tests still stop at the first hit. The tradeoff is an extra plane test on rays where the plane misses. The predicates retain the original thresholds and near-root semantics; the primary-ray path, 8x8 AO rays, and random draws remain unchanged.

retained: Add AO-only plane and sphere boolean predicates retaining the original plane parallel threshold, sphere D>0 condition, near root, positive-t condition, and 1e17 initial limit.
Test the plane before spheres and stop at the first confirmed occlusion, preserving the aggregate AO hit flag while avoiding unnecessary later tests.
Keep the original full intersection routines for primary rays and retain all 8x8 AO rays, random draws, and image updates.

trials.hypothesis: The earlier paired float paths were correct but their single three-sample means were slightly slower than baseline (3.488319 s for __builtin_sincosf and 3.479440 s for sincosf versus 3.477901 s). This contrasting test uses GCC's paired double-precision __builtin_sincos on the unchanged float phi, narrows the outputs before the existing float multiplications, and tests whether its distinct lowering offsets its extra precision cost. RNG calls, order, sample distribution, and count remain unchanged; speed and numerical effects are unmeasured.

retained: Replace float __builtin_sincosf(phi, ...) with double __builtin_sincos(static_cast<double>(phi), ...).
Narrow paired sine and cosine results to float before multiplying by the unchanged theta; leave sampling and all other code unchanged.

trials.hypothesis: The measured best candidate used cyclic static rows with worker-local PCG streams (0.4134 s); flattened static blocks of eight with worker-local streams were close (0.4152 s), while dynamic chunks with sample-indexed RNG were slower (0.4512 s) but confounded scheduling and RNG. This experiment holds the flattened static-8 schedule and one-thread serial path constant while replacing worker streams with counter-indexed SplitMix64 samples. It tests whether schedule-independent sampling changes correctness or runtime independently of scheduling; the additional hash work may cost more than worker-local PCG.

retained: Replace worker-local random streams with deterministic counter-indexed SplitMix64 values, converting the high 24 bits to uniform [0,1) samples for each of the 64 ambient rays.
Hold flattened pixel scheduling at static chunks of eight with the requested OpenMP thread count, and use a serial path for budgets of one or less or builds without OpenMP.
Accumulate each pixel locally and write all three channels exactly once while retaining every primary subsample and 8x8 ambient sample.

trials.hypothesis: The prior valid AO predicate candidates have close repeated means: 3.4749 s with all tests, 3.4643 s for the selected sphere-first predicate, and 3.4424 s for plane-first predicates, versus the 3.4779 s baseline. This candidate uses the original full Isect routines but stops after the first sphere hit and tests the plane only after sphere misses. It tests whether equivalent early exit can reduce traversal work while retaining Isect-update cost; the results must be measured before inferring a benefit.

retained: Replace AO-specific boolean intersection helpers with the existing full Isect sphere and plane intersection routines for ambient rays.
Stop sphere traversal after the first confirmed hit and test the plane only if all spheres miss; the accumulated AO hit flag is equivalent to testing every primitive.
Leave primary-ray intersections, random draws, all 8x8 AO rays, sample counts, and image updates unchanged.

trials.hypothesis: The selected parent keeps sample-indexed SplitMix64 sampling but assigns flattened pixels in static chunks of eight (0.452806 s). Earlier valid results were 0.413388 s for cyclic static rows with worker-local PCG and 0.415168 s for flattened static-8 with worker-local PCG; those comparisons change RNG as well as scheduling. This candidate keeps the parent's sample-indexed RNG and one-thread serial path, changing only work assignment to cyclic static rows, to test whether scheduling alone explains a runtime difference while preserving per-pixel samples.

retained: Keep counter-indexed SplitMix64 samples, keyed to primary-sample and ambient-ray indices, so sampling is unchanged by thread assignment.

Replace flattened static chunks of eight pixels with a cyclic static schedule over rows, with contiguous pixels rendered within each row; retain the serial row-loop path for thread budgets of one or less and for builds without OpenMP.
Preserve dimensions, subsample count, every primary and 8x8 ambient ray, and one complete write of all three image channels per pixel.

trials.hypothesis: Skipping the remaining AO primitive tests after a sphere hit may reduce traversal cost on the fast parallel T1 base. The AO result uses only the hit flag; the full set of primary and ambient rays and all random draws remain unchanged. The controller must measure the combined candidate.

retained: Retained T1's worker-local PCG32 streams, serial path for one or fewer threads, OpenMP cyclic row scheduling, complete per-pixel writes, and all required samples.

Adapted the selected T2 idea in ambient_occlusion: stop sphere traversal at the first hit and test the plane only when no sphere hit occurred. No AO rays, random draws, or primary intersections were removed or changed.

trials.hypothesis: A dynamic pixel schedule with chunks of 64 should balance spatially varying hit and ambient-occlusion work better than a static contiguous partition while keeping scheduling overhead bounded. Per-pixel SplitMix64 streams seeded from one serial draw should make samples independent of worker scheduling and thread count; the one-worker path avoids OpenMP overhead.

retained: Initialize one render seed serially from the caller's drand48 state, then derive independent per-pixel SplitMix64 streams.
Parallelize flattened pixel iterations with OpenMP dynamic scheduling in 64-pixel chunks and request no more than the supplied worker count.
Keep a direct serial loop for the one-worker case and preserve the primary sample and ambient-ray loop counts.

trials.hypothesis: Hoisting the per-call half-dimensions, aspect ratio, and subsample-count conversion out of the scalar primary-sample loops may remove repeated invariant work while preserving the order and values of the per-sample arithmetic. The compiler may already perform these hoists, so any benefit must be measured.

retained: Hoisted half-width, half-height, aspect ratio, and the floating-point subsample-count conversion to per-call setup; retained the primary-sample arithmetic order and per-ray image updates.

trials.hypothesis: Each ambient-occlusion hit uses the same ray origin for all 64 ambient rays, but the sphere intersection path recomputes each sphere-relative origin and its squared-distance term for every direction. Precomputing those invariant terms once per hit and using them only in ambient sphere tests should reduce repeated scalar intersection work; compiler hoisting and performance impact remain to be measured.

retained: Precompute each sphere's ambient-ray-origin-relative vector and quadratic origin term once per ambient-occlusion hit, then use a dedicated ambient sphere-intersection helper.
Leave primary sphere tests, scalar direction generation, random draws, plane intersection, all 64 ambient samples, and scheduling unchanged.

trials.hypothesis: Replacing three per-ray image read-modify-writes with one local scalar sum per pixel and three final channel stores may reduce memory traffic. The scalar receives each ret in the original sample order, as each original channel did from zero, so results should remain bitwise equivalent. To isolate this change against the original, this candidate restores the original inline primary-coordinate expressions rather than combining with the parent's explicit invariant hoisting. The compiler may hoist them automatically; correctness and performance need controller evaluation.

retained: Accumulate each pixel's ret values into one local float in the existing primary-sample traversal order.
Normalize the local scalar once and assign it to the three identical output channels once per pixel, replacing per-sample channel read-modify-writes.
Restore the original inline half-dimension, aspect-ratio, and subsample conversion expressions so this trial isolates local accumulation from explicit invariant hoisting.
Leave the ambient-occlusion ray-generation/intersection code, geometry, RNG sequence, and serial scanline scheduling unchanged.

trials.hypothesis: A cyclic static schedule over whole scanlines should reduce dynamic pixel-chunk scheduling overhead while distributing vertically varying row costs more evenly than contiguous row blocks. A direct nested loop for one requested worker avoids OpenMP team overhead; pixel-keyed SplitMix64 streams keep each pixel's random sequence independent of schedule and thread count. This contrasts with the previously valid dynamic-64-pixel candidate; relative performance remains unmeasured.

retained: Replace shared worker-side random draws with a serial render seed and deterministic, pixel-keyed SplitMix64 streams.
Parallelize scanlines with OpenMP schedule(static, 1), assigning each row to one worker; each worker writes only its row's pixel triplets.
Use direct x/y coordinates in the pixel routine, avoiding flattened-index division while retaining the existing projection and ray loop structure.
Keep a direct serial nested loop when the requested worker count is one, and cap the OpenMP team with num_threads(worker_count).
Preserve nsubsamples squared primary samples and all 64 ambient rays at each hit; keep the existing ao_serial and run interfaces.

trials.hypothesis: This isolates ambient azimuth direction generation: pairing the sine and cosine evaluation may reduce per-ray trig-call overhead without changing either random draw, the float azimuth, or the intended independent sampling distribution. The prior valid T3 variant measured 3.348743 s versus the baseline's 3.496109 s, but its cause and per-configuration performance are unknown; the catalog shows only one distinct T3 source program so far. No speedup or correctness result is claimed for this candidate.

retained: Add a paired-sine/cosine helper for the ambient azimuth using a compiler builtin on GCC/Clang and separate standard-library calls as the fallback.
Replace only the ambient-ray cosf(phi)/sinf(phi) pair with the helper; leave random draws, ray count, intersection work, primary-ray logic, and scheduling unchanged.

trials.hypothesis: Combining the prior invariant hoisting with local per-pixel accumulation may reduce repeated scalar setup and channel read-modify-writes, but the isolated results do not imply an additive gain: hoisting was only marginally faster than baseline, while accumulation alone was slower. The ordered float additions, primary-ray generation, AO kernel, RNG sequence, and scheduling remain unchanged; the controller should test the combination for all correctness cases and repeated timings.

retained: Hoist float half-width, half-height, aspect ratio, and subsample-count conversion to per-call setup while retaining the original primary-coordinate arithmetic order.
Accumulate each primary-ray result into one local float per pixel in the original subsample traversal order.
Normalize the accumulated scalar once and write the same resulting value to each of the three image channels once per pixel.
Leave AO ray generation/intersection, geometry, RNG calls and sequence, primary sample count/order, and serial scheduling unchanged.

trials.hypothesis: Static contiguous scanline assignment may improve row locality and reduce scheduling overhead compared with the prior cyclic static-row schedule, though it could balance vertically varying AO work less evenly than dynamic 64-pixel chunks. Both prior candidates were valid, with aggregate means of 0.46414 s for cyclic rows and 0.46135 s for dynamic chunks; those aggregates do not establish a per-configuration schedule advantage. A direct serial path avoids team overhead at one requested thread. Pixel-keyed SplitMix64 streams, initialized from one serial render-seed draw, should keep worker streams independent of schedule and thread count.

retained: Replace worker-side drand48 draws with one serial render-seed draw and a SplitMix64-derived stream keyed by linear pixel index.
Parallelize contiguous groups of scanlines with OpenMP schedule(static), bounded by num_threads(threads); retain a direct serial loop when threads is at most one.
Keep all primary-ray and 64 ambient-ray loop counts, existing ray math and per-pixel accumulation; each iteration writes only its own pixel triplet.

trials.hypothesis: The paired-sine/cosine variant measured 3.493764 s versus the 3.496109 s baseline, while the selected parent’s ambient-origin precomputation measured 3.348743 s; these aggregate results do not establish which ambient cost dominates. This separate experiment keeps the parent’s precomputation and sampling math but stores all 64 generated directions in structure-of-arrays form, then processes each sphere across independent ray lanes. The loops may expose intersection arithmetic to compiler auto-vectorization without ISA-specific code; whether that happens and whether it helps remain to be measured.

retained: Stage all 64 ambient directions in structure-of-arrays form while preserving original loop order, random draws, and direction calculations.
Evaluate each sphere across the independent ray lanes and update each lane's nearest positive root; then run the plane test across all lanes and count hits.
Leave primary-ray traversal, geometry, sample count, OpenMP scheduling, and all compiler/ISA configuration unchanged.

trials.hypothesis: Dynamic 16-pixel chunks may improve load balance over the measured dynamic-64 schedule when per-pixel hit and ambient-occlusion work varies, especially at high thread counts, but the extra scheduling overhead may offset that benefit. A direct serial path should avoid OpenMP team overhead at one thread. This tests chunk granularity against the valid dynamic-64 candidate; observed aggregate timings do not establish a per-configuration winner.

retained: Replace ambient-worker drand48 calls with per-pixel SplitMix64 streams seeded from a serial render-seed draw and linear pixel index.
Use OpenMP dynamic scheduling over flattened pixels with chunk size 16 and num_threads capped at the requested thread count; use a direct serial loop for one thread.
Preserve the primary-ray and ambient-ray counts, ray calculations, and one-pixel-per-worker output ownership.

trials.hypothesis: L’intégration combine les pixels indépendants et l’ordonnancement OpenMP de T1 avec le stockage SoA des directions ambiantes et les tests d’intersection par voie de T3. Les boucles par voie pourraient exposer les intersections au compilateur tout en gardant le parallélisme des pixels; les temporaires et le changement d’ordre des intersections peuvent aussi coûter davantage. Aucun gain additif n’est présumé, et le contrôleur doit valider toutes les tailles, graines et répétitions officielles.

trials.hypothesis: The baseline performs 2016 active backward updates per input after generating 64 terminal payoffs. Computing that sum should reduce the transition work to a linear pass. Repeated powers and binomial coefficients avoid dividing by Pu or 1-Pu, including when either probability is exactly zero. This is an unmeasured performance hypothesis; numerical tolerance and runtime remain for the controller to evaluate.
